nodes.name: BF cleaning and sensitization
nodes.procedure: Non-conducting BF substrate was cleaned with acetone and sensitized by 0.05 M SnCl2 and 0.12 M HCl for 30 min, followed by rinsing in DI water. The as-sensitized BF substrate was then dried.
nodes.source_text: Non-conducting BF substrate was cleaned with acetone and sensitized by 0.05 M SnCl2 and 0.12 M HCl for 30 min, followed by rising in DI water.

nodes.name: BF activation
nodes.procedure: The as-sensitized BF substrate was then activated in an aqueous mixture of 0.6 mM PdCl2 and 0.03 M HCl for 30 min, cleaned with DI water, and dried.
nodes.source_text: The as-sensitized BF substrate was then activated in an aqueous mixture of 0.6 mM PdCl2 and 0.03 M HCl for 30 min...

nodes.name: Electroless Co-P deposition on BF
nodes.procedure: To make the substrate conductive, the electroless deposition of CoP on activated BF was carried out at 70 °C for 30 min in CoSO4·7H2O and C6H5Na3O7·2H2O to which NaH2PO2 was added and adjusted to a pH of 10. The gray-colored conductive CoP–BF substrate was slowly washed with ethanol and DI water, and dried.
nodes.source_text: Finally, to make the substrate conductive, the electroless deposition of CoP on activated BF was carried out at 70 °C for 30 min...

nodes.name: CoMo electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: For the cathode, the freshly prepared conductive bare BF electrode was deposited with CoMo under ambient conditions in a 40 mL aqueous electroplating bath of 3.36 g CoSO4·7H2O, 1.92 g Na2MoO4·2H2O, and 3.52 g C6H5Na3O7·2H2O... A current density of 0.1 A cm−2 was applied for 20 min and the final product, the CoMo/Co–BF cathode, was washed with DI water and dried at 60 °C.
nodes.source_text: For the cathode, the freshly prepared conductive bare BF electrode was deposited with CoMo under ambient conditions in a 40 mL aqueous electroplating bath...

nodes.name: CoFe electrodeposition on Co-BF
nodes.procedure: The bimetallic CoFe alloy was deposited onto the conductive pristine BF electrode under ambient conditions using 0.1 M of FeCl2·4H2O and CoCl2·6H2O, each with 0.5 M KCl as the electrolyte. To avoid Fe2+ ion oxidation, the solution was purged with argon for 20 min while the pH was maintained at about 2.5–3. The deposition potential was set at −1.4 V for 15 min. The as-deposited CoFe/Co–BF electrode was washed with DI water and dried at 60 °C.
nodes.source_text: Similarly, for the anode, the bimetallic CoFe alloy was deposited onto the conductive pristine BF electrode under ambient conditions using 0.1 M of FeCl2·4H2O and CoCl2·6H2O...

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe/Co–BF shows uniform catalyst deposition of ~0.54 μm thickness masking smooth Co–BF surface with nanoparticle aggregation and spongy morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-deposited CoFe/Co–BF shows the uniform deposition of the catalyst layer to a few microns' thickness of about ∼0.54 μm (Fig. 1b and c), completely masking the smooth surface of the conductive bare BF substrate. The CoFe catalyst layer appears to be an aggregation of nanoparticles with a hierarchical thin spongy outer layer (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping confirms uniform distribution of Co and Fe elements in CoFe/Co–BF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy was employed to identify the presence of Co and Fe, and the elemental mapping given in Fig. 1d(i–iii) confirm the uniform distribution of Co and Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of CoFe/Co–BF show well-assigned fine Co peaks from Co–P-coated BF substrate and typical peak at 2θ = 44.4° corresponding to CoFe (111) plane with BCC structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The well-assigned fine Co peaks observed in the XRD patterns of the CoFe catalysts are attributed to the Co–P-coated BF substrate. The typical peak at 2θ = 44.4 corresponds to the CoFe (111) plane with a BCC structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of CoFe/Co–BF shows predominant Co²⁺ species in Co 2p scan and Fe³⁺ with characteristic multiplet in Fe 2p scan; metallic Fe⁰ peak at 706.5 eV indicates CoFe alloy presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p scan of CoFe/BF revealed the predominant presence of Co²⁺ species, whereas the Fe 2p scan of CoFe/BF showed the presence of Fe³⁺ with its characteristic multiplet... the existence of a metallic Fe⁰ peak at 706.5 eV still implies the presence of the CoFe alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of CoFe/Co–BF shows lattice fringes with d value of 0.201 nm corresponding to (100) plane of CoxFe1-xOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes observed from HR-TEM in Fig. 1h give a d value of 0.201 nm, which corresponds to the (100) plane of CoxFe1-xOOH obtained from the XRD patterns 2θ = 65).

nodes.characterization_summary: CoMo/Co–BF shows uniform catalyst deposition of ~0.5 μm thickness with hierarchical 3D nanostructure of orderly stacked nanoflakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CoMo/Co–BF also shows uniform deposition of the cathode layer to a few microns' thickness of ∼0.5 μm. The CoMo catalyst layer possesses a hierarchical 3D nanostructure, which appears like an orderly stacking of nanoflakes on the BF substrate (Fig. 2a and b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping identifies homogenous distribution of Co and Mo on CoMo/Co–BF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping in Fig. 2c(i–iii) evidently identifies the homogenous distribution of Co and Mo on the BF substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals intrinsic morphology and crystal structure of CoMo/Co–BF electrodes; SAED patterns show polycrystalline nature coinciding with hexagonal CoMo planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The intrinsic morphology and crystal structure of the electrodes were investigated by TEM (Fig. 2d). Similarly, the SAED patterns in Fig. 2e well-coincide with the corresponding planes of the hexagonal CoMo.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of CoMo/Co–BF shows distinct peak at 2θ = 40.54° corresponding to (200) planes of hexagonal CoMo; few visible peaks due to low Mo atomic ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distinct peak at 2θ = 40.54° correspond to the (200) planes of the hexagonal CoMo (Fig. X3(a–ii)) (JCPDF #29-0490). CoMo shows very few visible peaks because when the atomic ratio of Mo is comparatively low...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of CoMo/Co–BF shows metallic Co and Co²⁺ species indicating metallic CoMo alloy with surface oxidation; Mo 3d scan shows metallic Mo, Mo⁴⁺, and Mo⁶⁺ species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The deconvolution high resolution spectrum of CoMo/BF in Fig. 2f illustrates the presence of both metallic Co and Co²⁺ species... The Mo 3d scan (Fig. 2g) explicitly highlighted the presence of metallic Mo, MoO⁴⁺, and Mo⁶⁺ species...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS analysis shows negligible presence of Sn and Pd in CoFe/BF and CoMo/BF electrodes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of ICP-MS indicated the negligible presence of Sn and Pd in all the analyzed electrodes.
